correctness.rationale: The Schur norm formula for the main/upper diagonal mask is Levene 2014 Theorem 4.2, namely sigma_k=2/(k+1)cot(pi/[2(k+1)]) increasing to c=4/pi by Corollary 4.6. Exact multiplicativity under Kronecker products and supremum for Hilbert block-diagonal sums make the finite block norms a multiplicative monoid P, and bounded countable sums yield exactly bounded suprema of P. Let F={sigma_k:k>=2} union {c}; sigma_2=2/sqrt(3)>1 bounds the number of factors in any bounded product sequence, so compactness of F proves closure P equals all finite F-products and also equals union_m c^m P. For an accumulation point of this set, a sequence of distinct products with bounded factor number must have at least one factor tending to the only nonisolated element c, so S prime equals c S; conversely sigma_k p -> c p with distinct values. Repeated positive rescaling gives S^(m)=c^m S, and S^(omega) empty because each element of c^m S is at least c^m -> infinity. Each sigma_k is algebraic (cyclotomic cotangent) while c transcendental; c^m p cannot coincide with c^n q when m!=n and p,q positive algebraic, giving exact rank m, and no algebraic accumulation points, including at 2. This derivation is exhaustive and does not rely on a finite near-2 experiment.

value.rationale: The restricted path-generated norm family is mathematically natural because these are the explicit calculable nontrivial Schur idempotents and tensor/direct-sum are canonical operator constructions. A complete topological spectrum classification and algebraic isolation contrast with an unresolved accumulation question in the much larger full spectrum; the exact Cantor--Bendixson rank of every point is a useful structural invariant, not a mere near-numeric example.
residual_risks: The gap around 2 is qualitative, not effective, and cannot settle Levene’s unrestricted-spectrum open questions.

limitations: No all-idempotent Schur spectrum, no explicit epsilon at 2, and no independent exhaustive search of abstract product-derived-set theorem literature.
